gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a normal (Bluetooth Classic) headset can't use its mic while playing high-quality stereo. Microsoft's own explanation is that A2DP stereo 'doesn't allow the microphone to be used' and that HFP 'plays back audio in mono with lower fidelity'. Avoiding that on a PC takes either an LE Audio headset paired with an LE Audio-capable Windows 11 24H2 PC and an updated driver, or a maker's dongle such as the Jabra Evolve3 85's Link 390, which Jabra rates at 100 Hz–14.5 kHz super-wideband in call mode.
standout_why: SoundGuys' work-headphones list was cited in both chats. It says the Jabra 'comes with a USB-C Bluetooth adapter for your computer' and gives Bluetooth versions and codecs, but it never mentions HFP or hands-free mode, mono or lower-quality audio while the mic is on, or LE Audio/LC3. Three other pages ChatGPT got also never mention the hands-free/stereo split or LE Audio: SoundGuys' conference-call list, iTechGuides' 5 picks and SoundGuys' noise-canceling list. iTechGuides only warns that a wired Botesty's mic is 'not supported on desktops and certain laptops'. What Hi-Fi (cited in chat 2), both RTINGS pages and Tom's Guide gave only a title or navigation when fetched, so I could not check their article text. That is why this scores 2 and not 3.
decides: This changes the pick for a shopper who takes Zoom or Teams calls on a computer. Sony's own guide says the WH-1000XM6 has to be set to 'Headset (WH-1000XM6 Hands-Free)' (HFP/HSP) for both speaker and mic on a PC. On a Bluetooth Classic link that means mono, lower-fidelity playback during the call. Sony documents LE Audio pairing only for Android phones. The Jabra Evolve3 85 ships with its own Link 390 dongle and is rated 100 Hz–14.5 kHz SWB in speak mode, so it is the safer PC-call pick. Bose's QC Ultra 2nd Gen lists A2DP/HFP/AVRCP/BLE and no LE Audio, so its PC calls also go through hands-free mode. For phone-only use, all three work as ChatGPT described. Plugging in the XM6 cable doesn't avoid this: Sony says 'the Bluetooth function cannot be used' then, and calls are answered on the phone and spoken into the phone's mic.

findings.label: Why mic use lowers headphone audio on Bluetooth Classic
findings.value: A2DP 'provides high quality audio but doesn't allow the microphone to be used'; HFP 'allows the microphone to be used but plays back audio in mono with lower fidelity than A2DP'; original HFP codec 8 kHz sample rate, wideband doubled it but still mono
findings.source_title: Cutting the wire without cutting the audio quality – Windows OS Platform Blog (Microsoft), 26 Aug 2025

findings.label: What a PC needs for stereo while the mic is on (LE Audio super wideband stereo)
findings.value: Headset that supports Bluetooth LE Audio + Windows 11 PC that supports LE Audio + latest Windows 11 24H2 updates + updated Bluetooth audio driver from the PC maker
findings.source_title: Cutting the wire without cutting the audio quality – Windows OS Platform Blog (Microsoft)
findings.note: Microsoft notes that not every PC with Bluetooth LE also supports LE Audio.

findings.label: Device to select on a computer for video calls
findings.value: Speaker and mic: 'Headset (WH-1000XM6 Hands-Free)' (HFP/HSP); 'Headphones (WH-1000XM6 Stereo)' is for music playback (A2DP), and selecting it means 'a video call may not be available'
findings.source_title: Sony WH-1000XM6 Help Guide – Making a video call on your computer
findings.note: Sony's guide also says the headset 'may not work properly during a video call' depending on the computer or app.

findings.label: Bluetooth profiles and codecs

findings.note: TMAP/GMAP and LC3 are LE Audio profiles and codec.
